items.note: The page around the search is close to the reference: cream sidebar with an ink selected pill and dot, four saturated stat tiles with cream spot plates, ink pills on a ledge. But the focused search field keeps the same 2px warm-grey border it has at rest, so you can't tell it has focus. The reference marks focus with a clear blue ring (11-desktop).

The night version is carried well: navy page, indigo panels, white pills with ink labels, tiles that keep their hues (the 03-desktop palette). The focused search field still looks the same as at rest (lavender border, no yellow ring), so the state doesn't show.

Compact phone header: scrolling nav pills with area dots, then the search field, an ink search pill and an avatar circle. The language is clearly there, but the focused field looks exactly like its rest state, unlike the reference's blue focus ring.

The hovered table row fills with the cream subtle surface, as the reference does with tone and no border or lift. Table, ink filter pill with dot, and pill-framed status tags are all in the language. But the activity panel above is a tall blue field with one card and a nearly invisible ghost card, so the panel reads as empty.

Night palette held across sidebar, tiles and chart panel, with white pills on navy as in 03-desktop. The hover tone change is consistent with the light theme. The same half-built ghost card sits at the bottom of the blue activity panel.

The stacked phone layout keeps the stat tiles' hues, bold numbers and cream plates, close to the 08-desktop tiles. Pills keep their ledge. The hovered row is below the first screen, but the chrome is consistent with desktop.
The focused nav item gets a 2px blue ring that follows the pill shape, the same treatment as the reference's focus-visible pill (11-desktop). Clear and clearly in the system.
The dark theme swaps the ring to yellow on navy, a legible and deliberate equivalent of the reference's ring on night fields. Sits cleanly around the nav pill.
The focused cream nav pill gets the blue ring hugging its pill outline, well separated from the ink selected pill beside it. Reads the way the reference's focus state does.

The user chip darkens to its pressed cream tone and opens a white rounded menu with a soft float shadow, an email meta line and three generous text items. Calm and on-system, though plainer than the reference's crafted pieces.
The menu turns into an indigo panel with white labels, matching the night panels of 03-desktop. It reads clearly over the orange tile it overlaps.
On phone the menu drops under the avatar circle as a wide white card with large, touch-sized items. It covers the greeting, as a menu should. Clean and consistent with desktop.

The empty result is a cream panel with one blue zigzag glyph, a bold one-line title, a short sentence and one ink pill, and the filter field shows a blue focus border with a clear button. This is the spec's empty-state recipe and as tidy as the reference's cream panels (09-desktop).
The first screen shows the dark dashboard intact (navy, indigo chart panel, saturated tiles). The empty panel sits below the fold. It follows the same treatment as light.

The empty panel itself is good: cream, glyph, two-line title, ink pill. But the page above it carries a very tall blue activity field with one faded card and a large empty area, which crowds the page with a dead saturated block the reference never has.

Stat tiles become cream skeletons with a circle and pill-shaped lines, and the refresh pill shows the pop-dots glyph at its kept width. This is on-system and calm, with no spinner. No visible loading text tells the person what is happening.
Skeletons turn into indigo blocks on navy and the white pill shows ink pop dots. Consistent with light and in the night palette.
Phone skeleton tiles in a two-up grid with plate circles and line pills, and the pop-dots pill keeps its width. Clear and on-system.

Cream spot plates on each saturated tile hold pictograms of 2–3 primitives (a stack of pills, sun over hill, cloud with a drop, ring and dot), plus a yellow crescent with an orange sparkle beside the greeting. Each is distinct and on recipe. Close to the 07-desktop plates, if a little simpler in shading.

The blue header band ends in a proper sagging arc, with a crescent-shaded yellow disc, a white cloud and a pink sparkle in its trailing third. The pieces follow the kit, but they are spread thin, and the disc is cut off at the band's top edge. That is weaker than the reference's tight compositions of disc, cloud and sparkles (02-desktop).

The detail header band repeats the arc with a cloud and an orange sparkle. A yellow cover holds a crescent-shaded blue disc with a pink sparkle and a white dot, and a two-color yellow/pink disc stands on blue. Asymmetric, flat, on recipe, and close to the 06-desktop confetti discs.

The green header band has a crescent-shaded pink disc, a cloud and a yellow sparkle. Member avatars are bold initials on crescent discs rotating yellow, pink and orange, exactly as the spec's avatar rule says. Clean, but each is a small variation of the same disc.

Activity cards build one after another (opacity 0 → 0.4 → 1, short rise, 750ms). Header-band shapes fade in and one drifts slowly on an 8s loop; cloud and sparkle fade in. Calm, slow, no bounce, matching the spec's quiet illustration motion.

findings.summary: The dashboard's live activity list is built as a build-on-view vignette, so cards that haven't triggered stay invisible. A tall saturated panel shows one card and a faint ghost, or a large empty blue block on phones.
findings.promptFix: A vignette is an illustrative fragment, never the product's real data: a live feed, list or table of real records renders immediately and fully, with no build animation. A panel holding a short list sizes to its content instead of stretching to match a neighbouring column.
findings.specRule: Where. Hero and feature sections of front pages, onboarding and feature tours; ... a dashboard activity card.

findings.summary: The focused search field keeps its resting warm-grey border, so focus is invisible, while the spec asks for a 2px focus-ring border.
The loading state shows skeletons and pop dots but no visible loading text, so the person has only shapes to go on.

The header-band shapes are scattered thinly across the trailing area, and the main disc is cut off by the band's top edge. The reference groups disc, cloud and sparkles into one tight, overlapping composition.
